key_insight: The paper argues that warped geometry in AI-generated videos is largely a training-data problem: typical video datasets provide too few examples of how scenes should change as a camera moves.
problem_solved: Generated videos can distort structures, produce inconsistent parallax, and turn smooth camera movements into abrupt, shot-like transitions instead of preserving a coherent scene.
method: Identify a supervision gap: web-scale videos mostly show moving objects filmed by static or weakly moving cameras.
Focus on viewpoint-induced appearance changes as a source of training signal for geometric consistency.
Introduce an approach named “Video Geometry”; the supplied abstract ends before its implementation or evaluation is described.
impact: For video-generation practitioners, the paper highlights camera-motion coverage as an important dataset consideration. Better supervision of viewpoint changes could help models generate more spatially coherent videos, though results are not included in the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Side-by-side frame sequences showing a structure warping versus remaining consistent during camera movement.
A camera-path diagram illustrating viewpoint changes and foreground–background parallax.
A conceptual dataset comparison: moving objects with a static camera versus static scenes with a moving camera.
A continuous camera trajectory contrasted with abrupt shot-like transitions.
paper_title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
paper_authors: Weijie Lyu, Tiancheng Shen, Jason Li, Yujing Wang, Xiaoyuan Wang
